text:
The defending champions are not easing into this season. Carolina is 17-3-3 after Saturday's 7-4 comeback over Edmonton, 8-1-1 in its last ten, with points in six straight, and the underlying numbers are even better than the record. The Hurricanes have 60.5% of the expected goals (the quality of the chances) across all situations and 59% at five on five, the best kind of share in hockey. Our numbers project about 119 points, a 100% playoff chance and an 86% chance at the Metropolitan title.

They aren't living on luck either. Finishing is up about six goals on their chances and the goaltending about six goals better than the shots, modest edges for a team this dominant. The engine is depth. Sebastian Aho, Andrei Svechnikov and William Carrier have taken 66% of the chances together, and Nikolaj Ehlers, Logan Stankoven and Jackson Blake have been even better, 14 goals for and 1 against at five on five. Stankoven is running hot, 12 points in ten on 6.9 expected, which is more than his chances would normally return. Jaccob Slavin had Cory Lavalette of the North State Journal calling him "absurd" on Saturday.

What to watch: Jordan Staal is back from injured reserve and closing in on a milestone, and the only real worry is the shots that do get through. Pyotr Kochetkov allowed four on 15 against Edmonton.
